Hi Emily — thanks for outlining the questions. Quick summary up front, then details:

Summary (what we typically do)
- Standard approach: quarterly consumption checks with an annual true-up and settlement. Billing runs monthly on actual usage; true-up reconciles committed vs actual at quarter/annual checkpoint (depending on contract).
- Make-goods: credits are issued to cover shortfalls when we failed to provide committed capacity (rare). Customer-side underuse does not automatically generate make-goods credits — instead we offer limited reallocation or rollover policies depending on tier.
- Pilot carve-outs: we can offer a temporary carve-out for small pilots for the first two quarters, subject to an approval and cap.

Details
1) Quarterly vs annual: For your deal (D-98432-SP) we recommend quarterly reconciliation for transparency. Each quarter we compute: committed_tokens_for_quarter - actual_tokens_used. If negative (you used less), unused tokens are eligible for one of three paths: internal reallocation, rollover to next quarter (partial), or forfeiture. Final annual true-up reconciles any remaining delta and applies credits or charges per contract terms.

2) Reallocation rules (typical model):
- Within-account reallocation: permitted if teams are on the same legal entity and the seats/route are mapped in our Console. We can reassign up to 40% of unused quarterly commit to a different internal project within the same org by mutual agreement.
- Rollover: up to 25% of a quarter's unused commit may roll forward to the next quarter (once, not indefinitely).
- Forfeiture: remaining unused volume after reallocation/rollover is forfeited; no cash refunds except in exceptional negotiated cases.

3) Make-goods and credits:
- Make-goods are reserved for Redwood-side failures (downtime, SLA breaches). They are calculated as credits equal to the proportionate token cost for the impacted period.
- For customer underuse, we typically provide credits only in negotiated limited exceptions (e.g., enterprise commitments where usage modeling proved materially wrong).

4) Pilot carve-out: We can approve a 2-quarter carve-out capped at $10k/mo for StrataPulse as a one-time concession. It requires an addendum in the SOW and approval from Finance.

Action items
- Marissa: can you confirm the recommended reallocation % (40% / 25% rollover) is acceptable for the SOW?
- Emily: if you confirm the pilot carve-out, I'll loop in Legal for amendment language and share a SOW version.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30m call if helpful.

Best,
